The test `test_youtube_format_selection` checks whether the formats selection logic in the `YoutubeDL` class is correct, but it seems that this logic is flawed. 

Following the execution path, we find that the error occurs when the `process_video_result` method of the `YoutubeDL` class tries to select the requested format from the available formats. The issue lies in the line where it checks if there are any available formats:

```
if info_dict.get('formats') is None:
    # There's only one format available
    formats = [info_dict]
else:
    formats = info_dict['formats']
```

However, this logic is incorrect because even when there is only one format available (i.e., `info_dict['formats']` is not `None`), it still tries to select the requested format from the list of all available formats. This can lead to an empty list if the requested format is not in the list of all available formats.

The error message "requested format not available" suggests that this is indeed what's happening here. To fix this issue, we need to modify the logic so that it correctly handles the case when there is only one available format.

Let me know if you want me to suggest a solution!

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
